title: A Bayesian formulation of hybrid quantum-classical dynamics
abstract: We develop a Bayesian formulation of diffusive quantum-classical dynamics by treating the wave function and classical variables as components of an ordinary stochastic process. The joint probability density P(ψ,x,t) obeys a classical Fokker-Planck equation, while the quantum state appears as its second moment. Requiring this second moment to evolve linearly and autonomously yields the hybrid Lindblad equation and its stochastic unravelings. This construction makes positivity and unraveling freedom immediate and gives a unified description of quantum noise, classical noise, and their correlations through the covariance matrices (C,Γ,Q).   The same stochastic representation turns quantum-classical state estimation into a classical hidden-state inference problem. Filtering and smoothing are Bayesian conditioning on the observed classical trajectory. We recover the stochastic master equation from the Kushner-Stratonovich equation with correlated noise and show how the quantum effect operator is related to the Bayesian backward message through the adjoint dynamics of the linear unraveling. The Bayesian posterior also defines a smoothed density matrix and, more generally, a posterior distribution over latent quantum-classical trajectories.   These quantities can be approximated with standard particle filtering and smoothing methods. Numerical examples show that smoothing improves reconstruction of a hidden quantum-classical trajectory and that the full trajectory posterior can retain structure, such as multimodality, that is absent from its density-matrix second moment. The resulting framework connects quantum filtering, retrodiction, and smoothing to the standard forward-backward machinery of Bayesian time-series inference.
summary: This paper introduces a Bayesian formulation for hybrid quantum-classical dynamics, unifying the evolution of quantum and classical variables into a single stochastic framework. It derives the governing hybrid Lindblad equation and shows that quantum state estimation can be mapped onto a classical hidden-state inference problem. This allows the application of standard time-series tools like particle filtering to analyze quantum trajectories.
main_problem: The paper develops a rigorous Bayesian framework to describe and analyze diffusive quantum-classical dynamics, treating the joint evolution of the quantum state and classical variables.
main_result: It establishes that the dynamics can be unified under a hybrid Lindblad equation, and it recasts quantum state estimation into a standard classical hidden-state inference problem solvable via particle filtering and smoothing.
method: The core methodology involves deriving the joint probability density evolution via a Fokker-Planck equation and then applying Bayesian inference techniques (filtering and smoothing) to the resulting stochastic process.
model_or_system: The model describes open quantum systems interacting with classical variables, governed by a joint stochastic process $(\psi, x)$. The dynamics are characterized by noise covariances $(C, \Gamma, Q)$ and lead to the hybrid Lindblad equation.
key_observables: Filtered density matrix ($ho_F^t$), smoothed density matrix ($ho_S^t$), and the effect operator ($E_t$).
important_parameters: Noise covariance matrices $(C, \Gamma, Q)$, and the detector efficiency ($\eta_{	ext{eff}}$).
main_assumptions: The derivation of the key dynamics requires assuming that the noise parameters $(C, Q, \Gamma)$ are independent of the quantum state $\psi$, and that the evolution of the second moment ($ho_J$) is linear and autonomous.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the general stochastic evolution for the joint density, establishing the hybrid Lindblad form by imposing linearity constraints, and finally mapping the problem onto the established machinery of quantum filtering and smoothing via forward-backward Bayesian recursions.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, unified mathematical framework connecting quantum measurement theory (filtering/smoothing) directly to classical stochastic processes, which is highly relevant for modeling open quantum systems subject to continuous monitoring.
